title: WPMS/427/2005 of SUBHASH KAPOOR Vs ARUN HARI and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 427 of 2005
Sri Subhash Kapoor Ö Petitioner
Versus
Sri Arun Hari & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. M.C. Pandey, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Devesh Upreti, Advocate, present for the
respondents.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. This writ petition arises out of the proceeding of
civil suit being Original Suit No. 827 of 2002. The petitioner
was the plaintiff in the said suit. In the aforesaid suit his
application for amendment was rejected vide order dated
12.04.2005 by the learned Additional District Judge/F.T.C.-II,
Dehradun. Consequently, he filed the present writ petition
before this Court in which the operation and effect of the
aforesaid order was stayed by this Court vide order dated
04.05.2005. The matter was listed before this Court on
19.07.2013 and the writ petition was dismissed for non
prosecution. Subsequently the suit itself was dismissed for
non prosecution on 27.08.2014.
2. Now restoration application along with delay
condonation application has been filed for recalling the order
dated 19.07.2013 but on that day i.e. 22.09.2014 when the
matter was taken up, the application was dismissed for non-prosecution as the counsel for the petitioner has made a
statement before the Court that she has no instructions in the
matter. Today there is a new counsel before this Court, as the
earlier counsel Ms. Menka Tripathi has appeared before the
Court and she states that she has no instruction in the matter
and she wants to delete her name as a counsel for the
petitioner.
3. Heard Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. M.C. Pande, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.

2
Devesh Upreti, learned counsel for the respondents and
perused the record.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the
suit was restored on 28.10.2014. Therefore, he has filed the
present restoration application along with delay condonation
application. This application is being vehemently opposed by
the private respondents, who are represented by Mr. M.C.
Pande, Senior Advocate.
5. From the nature of the proceedings so far in this
matter before this Court, the conduct of the petitioner,
including the fact that his case was dismissed for non
prosecution on 19.07.2013 and thereafter a belated
application was made by him which was again dismissed for
non prosecution on the statement made by counsel for the
petitioner that she has no instruction and thereafter
restoration application has been filed again by the new
counsel.
6. The petitioner fails to inspire confidence. However,
purely in the interest of justice, on the principle that as far as
possible cases must be heard on its merit, the delay
condonation application is allowed. The delay in filing the
restoration application is hereby condoned and the order
dated 22.09.2014 is hereby recalled. Since the matter is
extremely old and in the interest of justice the delay
condonation application (No. 435 of 2014) as well as
restoration application (No. 6950 of 2014) also stands allowed.
Let the petition be restored to its original number.
7. The matter is now being heard on its merit. The
petitioner is a tenant in one of the shops, which are situated
at Rajpur Road, Dehradun. Adjacent to the shop of the

3
petitioner there are three other shops. The petitioner,
however, is a tenant in one of those shops. All the same,
according to him, he is using the roofs of all the four shops.
Admittedly the building in question comes under the purview
of Act No. 13 of 1972. For reasons best known to the
petitioner he filed a suit for injunction being civil suit No. 827
of 2002. The suit was filed on 10.12.2002 and after five
months an application for amendment was made on
22.05.2002. This application for amendment was dismissed
by the trial court vide its order dated 12.04.2005 against
which the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.
8. The order of the trial court has been perused. The
trial court states that not only such an amendment is not
liable to be allowed in view of the Order 6 Rule 17 of C.P.C.
but has given valid reason for doing so. According to the
petitioner, the suit itself was filed on 10.12.2002 the fact
which the plaintiff wants to insert by way of the existence at
the relevant time itself, he choose not to do so and now the
amendment has been sought purely in order to dilate the
proceedings. This Court has also examined as to what is the
amendment being sought by the petitioner in the plaint. It has
been mentioned that the petitioner claims to have been using
the roofs of the shops for the last so many years and since the
user being deprived of being using the roof he has filed the
suit for injunction. By way of an amendment he wants to
restore the possession of the premises. Since the relief the
petitioner was seeking by way of an amendment is already
there in the suit. Even if the amendment has been declined it
will not materially affect the case of the petitioner. Therefore,
the denial of the amendment seems be justified. One other
aspect, is that at the relevant time in the said suit an
application for temporary injunction was made by the

4
petitioner, which was rejected by the trial court on 17.12.2002
against which the petitioner filed an Appeal From Order No.
389 of 2002 which came up before the Division Bench of this
Court, in which the Division Bench of this Court while
dismissing the appeal passed following order:-
ìThe basis of the suit is user for about 40 years. If
in order to give some facility the defendants have
permitted the use the roof, which belongs to them, that
can not create any easementary right in favour of the
plaintiff on the basis of which he can maintain the suit.
Thus, in our opinion, the suit for the relief claimed is not
maintainable. Since we have come to the prima facie
opinion that the suit is not maintainable, therefore,
application under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 C.P.C. moved
in the suit was rightly rejected by the trial court.
Accordingly, we do not find any force in this appeal
which has been filed by the appellant against the order
of rejection of application under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2
C.P.C. No prima facie case having been made out in
favour of the plaintiff-appellant as discussed above the
appeal is devoid of merit and has to be dismissed.
The appeal is dismissed accordingly. No order as
to costs.î
 The petitioner, however, moved a review petition
against the above order in which the Division Bench passed
following order:-
ìOur order dated 11.06.2003 is modified to the
extent that our observation made in our judgment that
the suit is not maintainable shall not be read as bar for
the trial court for deciding the suit.
The application is disposed of accordingly.î
9. A finding, therefore, is also this Court that the suit
was not maintainable and later observation of the Court in the
review petition that the observation shall not bar the trial
court from deciding the suit does not help the case of the
petitioner, as all it states that the trial will decide the same on
its merits. The trial court while rejecting the amendment

5
application of the petitioner has taken note of the earlier
decision of this Court dated 11.06.2003 and has not noticed
the order dated 18.07.2003 passed by this Court in review
petition. The contention of the petitioner will not help him as
this Court is of the view that the application has been rightly
rejected by the trial court. No interference is liable to be
called for in the present writ petition.
10. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed. No
order as to costs.
11. However, having said this, the trial court is hereby
directed to dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible
without granting any unnecessary adjournment. It is made
clear that regarding the maintainability of the suit, the
defendant would be at liberty to raise all objections, including
maintainability of the suit itself, and if the trial court feels it
necessary shall make it as a preliminary issue and thereafter
proceed accordingly. Trial is expedited.
